policy: Conservative manually maintained ledger, supported by independent reviews that may be performed by AI agents. Add a certification only after the full named environment has source review, compiled actual exports and permitted transitive axioms. Partial components, algorithms and source obstructions do not count. All unlisted named environments remain uncounted. This is not a percentage of the entire monograph.

certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed two-clause convergence claim, arbitrary Q initialization and initial stationary randomized policy, all maximizing greedy tie choices, k>=1 and discount zero included. Fixed-point values are identified with actual trajectory Q by proved characterization and optimality theorems; no semantic certificate is assumed. The source lemma has no LaTeX label.

certified_named_results.statement_scope: Full fixed deterministic policy claim under the actual controlled trajectory law. The statement averages a stronger pointwise-in-initial-state export over an arbitrary initial distribution. No algorithm count, tie, optimism, or conditional variance-budget premise.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 5.3
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed deterministic max-one reciprocal-count bound, K>=2, with source episode-major sum order. The export and index generalize the algorithm-specific claim to every finite causal planner/path. First visits contribute one; no positive-visit, probability, bonus or concentration premise is added.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 5.11
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed profile-cardinality conclusion with K≥SAH log₂K, including K=1. Proved in stronger arbitrary finite episode-by-stage state-action row-table form, with the exact source threshold profile of pre-episode cumulative counts. A safe ceiling comparison family repairs the source intermediate inclusion (C15); the final printed bound is unchanged. This does not prove the printed intermediate family or the full MVP algorithm and regret bound.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 2.4
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed Hoeffding bound for N>0 i.i.d. draws and 0<δ<1, uniformly over a finite (possibly empty) random family of nonnegative vectors that is measurable and independent of the empirical row; the bound holds for every member with probability greater than 1−δ.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 2.5
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Both printed displays: the single-row Bernstein bound and the whole-matrix bound over all (s,a) with 4SA|𝒱|/δ, for rows with the correct i.i.d. law (any cross-row dependence allowed, so the independent generative model is included) and a random family independent of the empirical matrix. Trivially satisfied Nonempty premises are stated explicitly.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 2.10
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Both printed parts, each with both inequalities of its chain, for probability laws on an arbitrary measurable space, with p_e and p̄_e as infima over deterministic measurable tests. Part (iii) is commented out in the source. The printed premise β<1 is kept although unused.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 2.12
certified_named_results.statement_scope: KL divergence of finite product measures equals the sum of the coordinate KL divergences in ℝ≥0∞, for finitely many probability measures on arbitrary measurable spaces (indexed by any finite type, which includes the printed Fin n case and infinite values).

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 4.15
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed lower bound on E ξ with its Step-5 context written out and the existence of τ̂ part of the statement, for all t ≥ τ̂. Proved by a moment route instead of the printed Freedman step (C31).

certified_named_results.name: Theorem 5.19
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed statement: ∃ c₀>0 (witness 1/1536) such that for S≥2, A≥3, H≥2, K≥1 a finite family of episodic MDPs forces expected regret ≥ c₀·min{√(H³SAK), HK} for every history-dependent learner with a finite internal seed. Printed-proof gaps are recorded as C25–C27; the formal proof uses a direct adaptive-data KL chain rule.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 5.20
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed value-gap bound for the printed hard sub-MDP, H≥2 and 0<ε≤H/2 (the source's standing range).

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 5.21
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed testing bound: for A≥3 and t≤H³A/(18ε²), average next-arm error ≥1/3 for every history-dependent learner with a finite seed (a learner class containing the source's).

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 6.6
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed leave-one-out Bernstein bounds with printed constants for γ≥1/2, i.i.d. triples, every fixed point of T_pess, every pair with N_{s,a}>0 and every Ṽ in the printed ball, with probability ≥1−δ. The zero-count case is excluded because the printed bounds divide by N_{s,a} (statement-index scope disclosure); the printed-proof gap is repaired as in C23.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 6.18
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed fixed-row Bernstein bounds in conditional-on-counts form: for n=N_{s,a}>0 i.i.d. draws and V independent of the empirical row with 0≤V≤1/(1−γ), both bounds hold with probability ≥1−8δ for 0<δ<1/8.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 6.15
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed transition KL bound with explicit universal constant c₃=16·336² for every θ, θ̃, positive state and action under the construction's standing assumptions: 0 when θ_s=θ̃_s and at most c₃(1−γ)³ε² otherwise. The printed mis-citation of the Bernoulli KL step is recorded as C21; the conclusion is unaffected.

certified_named_results.name: Theorem 6.13
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed hypotheses and conclusion: ∃ c₂>0 such that for γ∈[2/3,1), S>12, C⋆>2, ε≤1/(672(1−γ)) there are S-state two-action instances with concentrability in [C⋆,2C⋆] on which every estimator has ρ-gap >ε with probability ≥1/4 when N≤c₂SC⋆/((1−γ)³ε²). Estimators may use an independent seed on any probability space (map from seed and the N i.i.d. samples to a stationary policy; probability under seed⊗data, the outer probability when the failure set is not measurable; no measurability premise); every Markov-kernel estimator is of this form. Deterministic estimators are the Dirac-seed case (Thm6_13, also proved). ε≤0 is handled as in C9.

certified_named_results.name: Theorem 6.3
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed theorem under its only coherent quantifier reading ∃c_b₀ ∀c_b≥c_b₀ ∃c₁ (witnesses 96 and 10⁴c_b; a c₁ uniform in c_b appears to fail): for γ∈[1/2,1), C⋆<∞, any Q⋆-greedy π⋆ and the printed sample-size condition, every greedy output policy is ε-optimal on ρ with probability ≥1−2δ. Lemma 6.7's restricted premises, Lemma 6.6's positive-count scope and C10/C19/C23 are discharged inside the proof.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 2.6
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed empirical Bernstein bound with the plug-in empirical variance, for N≥2 i.i.d. draws and 0<δ<1, uniformly over a finite (possibly empty) random family of nonnegative vectors that is measurable and independent of the empirical row, with probability greater than 1−δ. A deterministic family is the constant special case.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 2.7
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed lower and upper tails for n independent real Bernoulli(p) variables, 0<p≤1, on an arbitrary probability space: the lower tail for every a>0 and the 2·exp(−0.19τ) upper tail for every τ≥2pn; n=0 is allowed.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 2.11
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed reverse Fano bound for any probability laws P₀,…,P_M on an arbitrary measurable space and every M (including M=0), with the error infima taken over measurable tests; the second inequality is stated in ℝ≥0∞, which is equivalent to the printed real inequality when the KL sum is finite and trivially true when it is infinite.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 2.13
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Literal transcription for the Bernoulli KL expression of eq:defn-KL-bern: KL(p‖q) ≤ (p−q)²/(q(1−q)) for all 0<p,q<1, and KL(p‖q) ≤ KL(q‖p) ≤ (p−q)²/(p(1−p)) for 1/2≤q<p<1.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 3.6
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed residual bound on the event eq:Bernstein-empirical-optimal-value, for every empirically optimal deterministic policy (no tie rule fixed), every N>0 and every β₁≥0 (the source has β₁≥4, so less is assumed).

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 3.8
certified_named_results.statement_scope: All three printed clauses for 0<ε<1/(32(1−γ)) and γ∈[2/3,1): the parameter relations, the strict optimal-Q separation Q⋆_{M₁}(s₁,a)−Q⋆_{M₀}(s₁,a)>2ε for the actual source two-state MDPs, and the exact ratio identity and bound.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 4.9
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed weight bounds and identities under the source schedule with horizon T≥2 (needed for log T>0); γ≥0 and c₁≥c₂ are not assumed. The square-sum bound and the weight-sum identities are stated for every t, which is stronger than printed.

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 4.14
certified_named_results.statement_scope: All printed optimal V and Q values of the 4-state hard MDP with p=(4γ−1)/(3γ), for every 1/4<γ<1 (exactly the range where p∈(0,1)), including 1/(1−γp)=3/(4(1−γ)). Disclosed carrier choice: the source's state-dependent action sets are encoded with two actions per state, copies of the single action at states 0, 2 and 3; copies leave V⋆ and Q⋆ of the original actions unchanged (see C31 item 5).

certified_named_results.name: Lemma 5.17
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed learning-rate properties for η_n=(H+1)/(H+n), every H≥1: both 1/√n-weighted bounds and the square bound for every N≥1, and convergence of the tail series to 1+1/H (as a HasSum) for every n≥1.

certified_named_results.name: Theorem 4.7
certified_named_results.statement_scope: Printed statement, both cases: ∃ universal c₃, c_lb (16, 10⁻⁹) such that for γ∈[3/4,1), T≥c₃/(1−γ)², Q₀≡0 and either (i) η_t=1/(1+c_η(1−γ)t) for any c_η>0 or (ii) constant η∈(0,1), a 4-state 2-action MDP has max_s E|V_T(s)−V⋆(s)|² ≥ c_lb/((1−γ)⁴T log²T). Encoding disclosures: dominated dummy actions (C31), ∃s for the max, natural log, T∈ℕ, η 0 unused. The printed statement is proved. The book's own proof of case (i) is incomplete (C30); the Lean proof of case (i) is self-contained and does not depend on it. Case (ii) printed-proof slips repaired as in C31 (statement unchanged). Thm4_7_restricted, an earlier case (ii)-only entry, is implied by this one and kept for reference. Independently plan-checked and source-reviewed. Not author-approved.

Actual learner-family membership, corrected decoupling and corrected main regret are established separately by the later entries; this generic concentration theorem alone does not imply them.

proved_variants.name: Lemma 5.15, corrected MVP T6 variance bound

proved_variants.name: Lemma 5.14, corrected actual-law MVP decoupling

proved_variants.name: MVP main regret (corrected algorithm and confidence allocation)

I=40000(log2 K)^3 log(3SAH) log(1/delta-prime), delta-prime=delta/(100S^2A^2H^2K^2). The cases K = 1 and small K are proved directly; for large K the proof establishes its own eligibility conditions and accounts for the actual decoupling probability. Differs from the printed theorem in: the corrections of source issues C8, C12, C13, C15, C16 and C17 and a fixed tie-breaking rule, all stated explicitly. No extra probability or intermediate-bound premise is assumed. The source gives this result no theorem number, and none is assigned here.

Fixed deterministic maximizing tie and initial nonterminal V=H are disclosed in C20. Observed successor/count law and uniform concentration are proved, not additional hypotheses.

The claim at the printed allocation is neither proved nor refuted; the printed proof's use of Lemma 5.13 at l=1 is replaced by a deterministic argument (C16).

proved_variants.name: Theorem 5.1 (restricted tie-rule variant)
proved_variants.statement_scope: Restricted: both printed bounds, E Regret ≤ 8√(AT log(T²/δ)) and ≤ 10 log(T²/δ) Σ_{Δ(a)>0} 1/Δ(a), with exactly the printed hypotheses (2≤A≤T, means in [0,1], 0<δ<1) and i.i.d. The printed proof's Step 1 applies fixed-count tail bounds at a random count, which does not justify it under adaptive sampling (C36; the conclusion still holds); it is replaced by an adaptive Gaussian exponential-martingale tail (C36).

The proof conditions on the label sequence instead of the printed Azuma step (C28).

With ∃c_b₀ ∀c_b≥c_b₀ (the standing assumption of Lemma 6.9 and Theorem 6.8), Q_t≤Q⋆ and V_t≤V^{π_t}≤V⋆ hold with probability >1−δ, for tie rules depending only on the Q-row.

The existential guarantee is proved from scratch with an explicit reconstructed witness: optimistic Hedge (entropic FTRL) with backward induction and per-agent adaptive generative queries. The witness is not shown to be Q-FTRL, and it is not model-based (it builds no empirical transition kernel). With one universal constant C = 20000, quantified before all sizes, for every δ ∈ (0,1), ε ∈ (0,H], known reward (bounded on steps 1..H) and every transition kernel, with probability ≥ 1−δ: (i) N ≤ C·H⁴S·Σ_iA_i·ε⁻²·log(4HSΣ_iA_i/δ) adaptive, randomized generative queries give an ε-CCE (joint output, gap ≤ ε); (ii) for two-player zero-sum games (r₂ = −r₁, r₁ ∈ [0,1]), N ≤ C·H⁴S·A·ε⁻²·log(8HSA/δ) queries give an ε-NE product policy, with A read as max(A₁,A₂), which implies the A₁+A₂ and A₁ = A₂ readings. The query count is deterministic; Õ is read as a universal constant times one log(·/δ) factor with no ε in the logarithm. The algorithm sees the reward but not P. Adds the domain binders S ≥ 1 and A_i ≥ 1. The two clauses are separate existentials sharing C; that one algorithm serves both is argued in prose only. Whether Q-FTRL itself attains the rate is not checked. Not author-approved; this does not prove the printed theorem.
